title: Positivity of a phase contract
statement: Let $I$ index a family of machines with phase state sets $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$, let $q_0$ be a state of the phase-host machine, and let $red$ assign to each phase and state either no successor or a state in the disjoint union of the phase state sets. Fix a phase $p$, a state $s_0\in\mathrm{Ph}(p)$, and a contract $C$ for the machine in phase $p$. Suppose the halted state is not in $C$'s exit set; every state outside that exit set reduces to no successor in phase $p$; and every state in that exit set reduces to a state in a different phase. If $C$ has strictly positive assigned time for every eligible datum and starting configuration, then the contract obtained by placing $C$ inside the phase-host machine has strictly positive assigned time for every eligible datum and starting configuration.
hypotheses_covered: A family of phase-indexed machines and their phase state sets
A fixed phase $p$ and entry state $s_0$
$C$ is a contract for the phase-$p$ machine
The halted state is outside $C$'s exit set
Every state outside the exit set reduces to no successor
Every state in the exit set reduces to a state in a different phase
$C$ has strictly positive assigned time for every eligible datum and start
replaced:
Let $M_p$ be the machine for phase $p$ in a family of phase-indexed machines, let $C$ be
a contract for $M_p$, and let $q_0$ be a state of the phase-host machine. Suppose the
reduction map sends every state outside the exit set to no successor, sends every state
in the exit set to a successor in a different phase, and the halted state is not in the
exit set. If $C$ has strictly positive duration on every entry-state configuration
satisfying its precondition, then the contract obtained by placing $C$ inside phase $p$
of the host machine has strictly positive duration.
